q.s: The Harappan outpost of Shortughai in northern Afghanistan was mainly associated with the trade in:
q.x: Shortughai lay near the Badakhshan mines and served as a Harappan outpost for lapis lazuli; Nageshwar was a shell-working centre.

q.s: The presence of identical weights across the Harappan region, pointing to regulated trade, shows that the Harappan weights followed a system based mostly on multiples of:
q.x: Harappan weights were mostly cubical chert weights following a binary system in multiples of 16 for smaller units; the same standard was used over about 8,00,000 sq km.

q.s: Ochre Coloured Pottery (OCP) culture, often found along with the Copper Hoards, represents the Late Harappan phase of which region?
q.x: OCP marks the Late Harappan phase of the Ganga–Yamuna Doab and is often associated with the Copper Hoards.

q.s: Which Harappan site has so far yielded ancient DNA from a human skeleton?
q.x: A skeleton from Rakhigarhi (Haryana) is the only Harappan sample so far to yield ancient DNA.

q.s: India's national motto 'Satyameva Jayate' is taken from which Upanishad?
q.x: 'Satyameva Jayate' comes from the Mundaka Upanishad; 'Tat tvam asi' is from the Chandogya.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of Upanishadic saying/story and source is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Nachiketa–Yama dialogue is in the Katha Upanishad; the other three pairs are correct.

q.s: The Shatapatha Brahmana belongs to which Veda?
q.x: The Shatapatha Brahmana is attached to the Shukla (White) Yajurveda; the Gopatha is the only Brahmana of the Atharvaveda.

q.s: Which is the only Brahmana attached to the Atharvaveda?
q.x: The Gopatha is the sole Brahmana of the Atharvaveda; Aitareya and Kaushitaki belong to the Rigveda, Jaiminiya to the Samaveda.

q.s: The famous Ajanta painting known as the 'Dying Princess' is found in which cave?
q.x: The Dying Princess is in Cave 16; Cave 1 has the Bodhisattva Padmapani.

q.s: The later paintings of Ajanta, such as those of Caves 16 and 17, belong to the period of which dynasty?
q.x: The later Ajanta caves and paintings were made under Vakataka patronage (5th century CE).

q.s: According to the Ajivika sect founded by Makkhali Gosala, the course of life is decided by:
q.x: The Ajivikas held that Niyati (destiny) governs everything and karma cannot alter it.

q.s: Kharavela, the famous Jain ruler of Kalinga, belonged to which dynasty?
q.x: Kharavela of the Chedi or Mahameghavahana dynasty is known from the Hathigumpha inscription at Udayagiri.

q.s: Chamundaraya, who got the Gommateshwara statue made at Shravanabelagola, was a minister of which dynasty?
q.x: Chamundaraya was minister of the Western Ganga ruler Rachamalla IV.

q.s: According to Megasthenes, the city of Pataliputra was administered by:
o: Five committees of six members each
Six committees of five members each
Four committees of eight members each
q.x: Megasthenes' Indica describes six committees of five members each running Pataliputra.

q.s: Megasthenes called the Mauryan town officials:
q.x: He called town officials Astynomoi and district officials Agronomoi.

q.s: In Mauryan administration, the Gopa was an officer in charge of:
q.x: The Gopa kept accounts for a group of 5–10 villages; the Sthanika collected taxes over a larger division.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT an official of Mauryan administration?
q.x: Amaranayakas were Vijayanagara military chiefs; Pradeshika, Sthanika and Gopa were Mauryan officers.

q.s: Ashoka's Rummindei pillar inscription records his visit to:
q.x: The Rummindei pillar records Ashoka's visit to Lumbini, the Buddha's birthplace, and the reduction of tax there.

q.s: Which one of the following statements about Ashoka's pillar inscriptions is correct?
o: The Rummindei pillar records his visit to Bodh Gaya
Pillar Edict VII is found on all Ashokan pillars
Pillar Edict VII is found only on the Delhi–Topra pillar
Pillar Edict VII says Dhamma spreads better by law than by persuasion
q.x: Pillar Edict VII is only on the Delhi–Topra pillar and says Dhamma spreads better by persuasion; Rummindei records the Lumbini visit.

q.s: Ashoka donated the Barabar caves in Bihar to which sect?
q.x: Ashoka gave the Barabar caves to the Ajivikas; his grandson Dasaratha gave the Nagarjuni caves.

q.s: The Gudimallam linga, the earliest known Shiva linga, is located in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Gudimallam is near Renigunta in Tirupati (old Chittoor) district; the linga dates to about the 2nd–1st century BCE.

q.s: The 'Kalingattuparani', celebrating the Kalinga war of Kulottunga I, was written by:
q.x: Jayamkondar wrote the Kalingattuparani; Kamban wrote the Tamil Ramayana.

q.s: Which Chola ruler abolished tolls and was called 'Sungam Tavirtta Chola'?
q.x: Kulottunga I abolished tolls, earning the title Sungam Tavirtta Chola; he also sent 72 merchants to China in 1077.

q.s: The Uttaramerur inscriptions, which describe the working of Chola village assemblies, belong to the reign of:
q.x: The Uttaramerur inscriptions on sabha elections date from Parantaka I's reign.

q.s: In the battle of Takkolam (949 CE), the Chola ruler Parantaka I was defeated by:
q.x: The Rashtrakuta Krishna III defeated Parantaka I at Takkolam in 949.

q.s: Which of the following rulers did NOT belong to the Mamluk (Slave) dynasty of Delhi?
q.x: Jalaluddin Khalji founded the Khalji dynasty in 1290; Aibak (Qutbi line), Iltutmish (First Ilbari) and Balban (Second Ilbari) were Mamluks.

q.s: Which of the following ruler–reign pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Bahlol Lodi ruled 1451–1489; 1526 is when Ibrahim Lodi lost at Panipat.

q.s: Vasco da Gama reached Calicut in 1498 during the reign of which Delhi Sultan?
q.x: Sikandar Lodi ruled 1489–1517, so Vasco da Gama's 1498 arrival fell in his reign.

q.s: The Moth ki Masjid in Delhi was built during the reign of:
q.x: Moth ki Masjid was built by Sikandar Lodi's minister Wazir Miyan Bhoiya.

q.s: Muhammad bin Tughlaq sought investiture from the Abbasid Caliph based at:
q.x: The Baghdad Caliphate ended in 1258; the Abbasid line continued in Cairo (Egypt), from where Muhammad bin Tughlaq sought recognition.

q.s: Which Sultan of Delhi proclaimed himself Caliph, taking the titles 'Al-Imam' and 'Khilafatullah'?
q.x: Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah Khalji declared himself Caliph, the only Delhi Sultan to do so.

q.s: In 1686, the first armed clash between the Mughals and the English took place when the English under Job Charnock were driven out of Hooghly by:
q.x: Shaista Khan, Aurangzeb's governor of Bengal, drove Charnock out of Hooghly in 1686 (Child's War).

q.s: The Zabti or Dahsala system of land revenue under Akbar was introduced by:
q.x: Todar Mal's Dahsala (1580) fixed cash rates on the average produce and prices of ten years, based on measurement.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a method of land revenue assessment under the Mughals?
q.x: Ryotwari was a British settlement of the Madras and Bombay Presidencies; Zabti, Batai and Kankut were Mughal methods.

q.s: Which Mughal emperor was blinded and deposed by Imad-ul-Mulk in 1754?
q.x: Ahmad Shah was blinded and deposed in 1754; his successor Alamgir II was later murdered by Imad-ul-Mulk (1759).

q.s: The Battle of Plassey (1757) was fought during the reign of which Mughal emperor?
q.x: Alamgir II reigned 1754–59, so Plassey fell in his reign.

q.s: The autonomous state of Hyderabad was founded by:
q.x: Nizam-ul-Mulk, a Turani noble, founded Hyderabad (1724); the Irani Saadat Khan founded Awadh.

q.s: Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib in Chandni Chowk, Delhi marks the place where which Sikh Guru was executed?
q.x: Guru Tegh Bahadur was beheaded at Chandni Chowk in 1675 on Aurangzeb's orders.

q.s: Which one of the following statements about Ramanuja is correct?
o: He worked at Srirangam and propounded Vishishtadvaita
q.x: Ramanuja, called Ilaya Azhwar and held to be an incarnation of Adisesha, opposed Advaita; Madhva taught Dvaita and Basava led the Virashaivas.

q.s: Which social practice was encouraged by the Virashaivas (Lingayats) who rejected Brahmanical rules?
q.x: The Virashaivas rejected caste and ritual and encouraged post-puberty marriage and widow remarriage.

q.s: 'India Wins Freedom' is the autobiography of:
q.x: Azad wrote India Wins Freedom; Rajendra Prasad wrote India Divided and Lajpat Rai wrote Unhappy India.

q.s: Which of the following book–author pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: India Wins Freedom – Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
q.x: 'Living an Era' is by D.P. Mishra.

q.s: Following the recommendations of which commission was a single Indian Army with four commands formed in 1895?
q.x: The Eden Commission (1879) recommended reorganisation, leading to the unified Indian Army with four commands in 1895.

q.s: At the time of the Battle of Plassey, Mir Jafar held which post under Siraj-ud-daula?
q.x: Mir Jafar was Mir Bakshi; Rai Durlabh was Diwan. Mir Madan and Mohan Lal stayed loyal to Siraj.

q.s: Which of the following did NOT join the conspiracy against Siraj-ud-daula before Plassey?
q.x: Mir Madan and Mohan Lal stayed loyal to Siraj; Mir Jafar, Rai Durlabh, Jagat Seth and Omichund were in the plot.

q.s: Ranjit Singh's army was trained on European lines by the French generals:
q.x: Ventura and Allard trained the Fauj-i-Khas, the model brigade of Ranjit Singh's army.

q.s: Who was the last ruler of the Sikh kingdom of Punjab?
q.x: Duleep Singh, under the regency of Rani Jindan, was the last ruler; Punjab was annexed in 1849.

q.s: Which one of the following statements about the impeachment of Warren Hastings is correct?
o: It ended in his conviction in 1795
It was led by Edmund Burke and ended in his acquittal in 1795
It was led by Lord North
The judicial murder of Nand Kumar was not one of the charges
q.x: Burke led the impeachment; Nand Kumar's case was among the charges; Hastings was acquitted in 1795.

q.s: Komaram Bheem led the Gond tribal movement in the Nizam's Hyderabad State during:
q.x: Komaram Bheem's struggle (slogan 'Jal, Jangal, Zameen') ran from about 1938 until his death in 1940 at Jodeghat.

q.s: The Rampa rebellion of 1922–24 was led by:
q.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju led the Rampa (Manyam) rebellion of 1922–24; Pulikantha Sambaiah led the 1879 Rampa revolt.

q.s: The Indian Universities Act of 1904 was passed during the viceroyalty of:
q.x: Curzon passed the Universities Act (1904) on the Raleigh Commission's report.

q.s: Which of the following measures was NOT introduced during Lord Lytton's viceroyalty?
q.x: The Ilbert Bill (1883) came under Lord Ripon; the other three belong to Lytton's time.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Ryotwari system?
o: The ryot paid revenue directly to the State
The ryot could sell, mortgage or lease his land
A zamindar collected revenue as an intermediary
The assessment was revised about every 30 years
q.x: Ryotwari had no zamindar intermediary; that was the Permanent Settlement. Ryotwari assessment was revised about every 30 years.

q.s: G.N. Taylor, who started an Anglo-Vernacular School at Narsapur in 1852, is known for drafting the:
q.x: Taylor framed the Godavari District Education Scheme of 1854 and opened schools at Narsapur and nearby towns.

q.s: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was an agreement between:
o: The Congress and the British Government
Moderates and Extremists of the Congress
The Congress and the Muslim League
The Muslim League and the Hindu Mahasabha
q.x: The Lucknow Pact united the Congress and the League; with the Khilafat–Non-Cooperation movement it marks the high point of unity (1916–22).

q.s: Who was the first High Commissioner for India in London, appointed under the Government of India Act, 1919?
q.x: Sir William Meyer was the first High Commissioner (1920); Simon later headed the Statutory Commission of 1927.

q.s: Which one of the following statements about the Government of India Act, 1919 is correct?
o: It introduced dyarchy at the Centre
It made the central legislature bicameral
It gave full autonomy to the provinces
q.x: The Act created the Council of State and Legislative Assembly; dyarchy was in the provinces and communal electorates were extended to Sikhs and others.

q.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, residuary powers were vested in the:
q.x: Residuary powers lay with the Governor-General; the Act had Federal, Provincial and Concurrent lists.

q.s: Which of the following lists was NOT provided in the Government of India Act, 1935?
q.x: The Act had Federal (59), Provincial (54) and Concurrent (36) lists; residuary powers were left to the Governor-General.

q.s: The Self-Respect Movement (1925), which popularised marriages without priests, was founded by:
q.x: Periyar founded the Self-Respect Movement in 1925; self-respect marriages were held without Brahmin priests.

q.s: Kandukuri Veeresalingam was called the 'Vidyasagar of South India' by:
q.x: M.G. Ranade gave him the title for his work for widow remarriage and women's education.

q.s: Veeresalingam founded the Widow Remarriage Association in 1880 at:
q.x: The association was founded at Rajahmundry in 1880; he opened a widow home at Madras in 1897.

q.s: The Faraizi Movement of Bengal was founded in 1818 by:
q.x: Haji Shariatullah founded the Faraizi movement; his son Dudu Mian made it agrarian.

q.s: The Ahmadiyya Movement was founded in 1889 at:
q.x: Mirza Ghulam Ahmad founded the Ahmadiyya movement at Qadian (Punjab) in 1889.

q.s: The Namdhari (Kuka) movement among the Sikhs was led by:
q.x: Baba Ram Singh led the Namdhari movement; Baba Dayal Das founded the Nirankari movement.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a Sikh reform movement?
q.x: Prarthana Samaj was a Hindu reform body of Bombay (1867).

q.s: The partition of Bengal announced by Lord Curzon came into effect on:
q.x: It took effect on 16 October 1905, observed as a day of mourning; it was annulled in 1911.

q.s: The boycott resolution that formally launched the Swadeshi Movement was passed at the Calcutta Town Hall on:
q.x: The boycott resolution was passed at the Calcutta Town Hall on 7 August 1905.

q.s: W.C. Rand, the plague commissioner, was assassinated at Poona in 1897 by:
q.x: Damodar and Balkrishna Chapekar shot Rand in 1897.

q.s: The Ramosi peasant force was organised in Maharashtra in 1879 by:
q.x: Phadke raised the Ramosi force in 1879 to fight British rule.

q.s: The Anushilan Samiti was founded in 1902 at Calcutta by:
q.x: Pramathanath Mitra founded it at Calcutta; the Dhaka branch was led by Pulin Behari Das.

q.s: Which one of the following statements about the Ghadar movement is correct?
o: The Ghadar Party was founded at London
Its planned revolt of 21 February 1915 was foiled by treachery
Kartar Singh Sarabha was acquitted in the Lahore Conspiracy Case
The Defence of India Act was passed in 1919
q.x: The 1915 rising was betrayed; the party was founded at San Francisco (1913); Sarabha was hanged; the Defence of India Act came in March 1915.

q.s: The Chauri Chaura incident of February 1922, which led Gandhi to withdraw the Non-Cooperation Movement, took place in which present district?
q.x: At Chauri Chaura (Gorakhpur district), a crowd burnt the police station, killing 22 policemen.

q.s: Mahatma Gandhi presided over the Indian National Congress only once, at its session held at:
q.x: Gandhi presided over the Belgaum session in 1924.

q.s: Which of the following Congress session–President pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Gandhi presided at Belgaum (1924), his only presidency; Sarojini Naidu presided at Kanpur (1925).

q.s: Madduri Annapurnaiah, who led the Forward Bloc in Andhra, was jailed for his writings in the journal:
q.x: Annapurnaiah was jailed for 18 months for 'Chicharapidugu' and led the Forward Bloc in Andhra with Peta Bapayya.

q.s: Which one of the following statements about the Interim Government of 1946 is correct?
o: It was headed by Mahatma Gandhi as President
The Muslim League refused to join it at any stage
It was sworn in on 2 September 1946 with Nehru as Vice-President of the Executive Council
It was formed under the Wavell Plan of 1945
q.x: The Interim Government took office on 2 September 1946 with Nehru as Vice-President and Wavell as President; the League joined on 26 October 1946. It followed the Cabinet Mission Plan.

q.s: Which businessman, long the treasurer of the AICC, was called Gandhi's 'fifth son'?
q.x: Jamnalal Bajaj, a cotton merchant and banker of Wardha, served as AICC treasurer and was adopted by Gandhi as his 'fifth son'.

q.s: The title 'Deen Bandhu' was given by Gandhi to:
q.x: C.F. Andrews was called Deen Bandhu; C.R. Das was Deshbandhu.

q.s: Which of the following titles is NOT correctly matched with the person?
q.x: 'Bihar Kesari' was Sri Krishna Sinha, first Chief Minister of Bihar, not Rajendra Prasad.

q.s: To suggest political reforms in Hyderabad State in the late 1930s, the Nizam appointed the:
q.x: The Aravamudu Iyengar Committee was set up by the Nizam to suggest reforms; the Hyderabad State Congress was banned in September 1938.

q.s: 'The Story of the Integration of the Indian States' was written by:
q.x: V.P. Menon, Secretary of the States Ministry, wrote it; K.M. Munshi wrote 'The End of an Era' on Hyderabad.

q.s: Which of the following books on Hyderabad and integration is NOT correctly matched with its author?
o: The Story of the Integration of the Indian States – V.P. Menon
The End of an Era – V.P. Menon
The Saga of Hyderabad Struggle – Swami Ramananda Tirtha
The End of an Era – K.M. Munshi
q.x: 'The End of an Era' was written by K.M. Munshi, India's Agent-General in Hyderabad.

q.s: The creation of a separate province of Bihar and Orissa, which encouraged the demand for an Andhra province, was announced at the Delhi Durbar of:
q.x: The Delhi Durbar of 12 December 1911 annulled the partition of Bengal and announced a separate Bihar and Orissa (formed 1912).

q.s: The first conference that discussed a resolution for a separate Andhra province was held in May 1912 at:
q.x: The Nidadavolu conference (May 1912) of Godavari, Krishna and Guntur saw the first separate-province resolution; the first Andhra Mahasabha met at Bapatla in 1913.

q.s: Bhairavakonda, a Saiva centre with eight rock-cut cave temples, is located in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Bhairavakonda is in Nellore district.

q.s: The Naneghat inscription, one of the earliest Satavahana records, was issued by:
q.x: Naganika, queen of Satakarni I, issued the Naneghat inscription in Maharashtra; Gautami Balasri issued the Nasik prasasti.

q.s: Which Satavahana ruler is known for coins bearing the figure of a ship?
q.x: Yajnasri Satakarni, greatest of the later Satavahanas and patron of Acharya Nagarjuna, issued ship-type coins.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a Satavahana ruler?
q.x: Kharavela was the Chedi ruler of Kalinga.

q.s: Which Roman writer complained in his 'Natural History' about the drain of Roman gold to India?
q.x: Pliny the Elder recorded the drain of Roman gold to India; he also quoted Megasthenes on the Andhras' 30 walled towns.

q.s: Which of the following is the notable rock-cut Buddhist site of the eastern Deccan, where most monuments were structural?
q.x: Guntupalli has rock-cut chaitya and viharas; Amaravati, Nagarjunakonda and Bhattiprolu are structural stupa sites.

q.s: Which one of the following statements about rock-cut architecture of the Satavahana age is correct?
o: Amaravati is a rock-cut cave site
The Karle chaitya is in the eastern Deccan
Rock-cut activity peaked in the Eastern Ghats
The Bhaja caves are earlier than the Karle chaitya
q.x: Rock-cut work peaked in the Sahyadris of the western Deccan, where Bhaja is earlier than Karle; Amaravati is a structural stupa.

q.s: The Vishnukundin king Madhava Varma II married a princess of which dynasty?
q.x: The Khanapur plates record his marriage to a daughter of the Vakataka king; he performed 11 Ashvamedhas.

q.s: Kubja Vishnuvardhana, founder of the Eastern Chalukya line of Vengi, was the brother of:
q.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana ruled Vengi as Pulakesin II's representative (Kopparam inscription) and founded the Eastern Chalukya dynasty.

q.s: Renadu, the home region of the Renati (Telugu) Cholas, lay in the upper basin of which river?
q.x: Renadu lay where the Kadapa, Kurnool and Chittoor regions meet, in the upper Pennar basin.

q.s: 'Kridabhiramamu' of Vinukonda Vallabharaya depicts the social life of which city?
q.x: Kridabhiramamu describes life in the Kakatiya capital Orugallu.

q.s: The Gajapati ruler who annexed the Reddi kingdom of Rajahmundry in the 1440s was:
q.x: Kapileswara Gajapati annexed Rajahmundry in 1446–48, ending the Reddi kingdom.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a capital of the Reddi kingdoms?
q.x: The Reddis ruled from Addanki, Kondavidu and Rajahmundry; Warangal was the Kakatiya capital.

q.s: In the Gajapati administration of Orissa, a 'Dandapata' denoted:
o: A large province with a standing army
q.x: A Dandapata was a large province (whole districts) with a standing army; Naidus were revenue officers of the Telugu regions.

q.s: The Raichur Doab, contested by Vijayanagara and the Bahmanis, lay between the rivers:
q.x: The Raichur Doab is the fertile land between the Krishna and the Tungabhadra.

q.s: The Charminar at Hyderabad was built in 1591 by:
q.x: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah built the Charminar (1591–92) when founding Hyderabad.

q.s: Which of the following monuments was NOT built by the Qutb Shahi rulers?
q.x: Gol Gumbaz at Bijapur is the tomb of Muhammad Adil Shah of the Adil Shahis.

q.s: Harihara and Bukka founded the Vijayanagara kingdom in 1336 under the inspiration of:
q.x: The sage Vidyaranya (Madhava) of Sringeri is traditionally credited with inspiring the founders.

q.s: In the Battle of Raichur (1520), Krishnadevaraya defeated:
q.x: Krishnadevaraya routed Ismail Adil Shah of Bijapur at Raichur in 1520, with Portuguese help.

q.s: In his Kalinga campaign (1513–19), Krishnadevaraya fought against the Gajapati ruler:
q.x: Krishnadevaraya's army reached Cuttack and Prataparudra Gajapati sued for peace, giving his daughter in marriage.

q.s: 'Madhura Vijayam', describing Kumara Kampana's conquest of Madurai, was written by:
q.x: Gangadevi, Kampana's queen, wrote the Sanskrit poem Madhura Vijayam.

q.s: Which of the following work–author pairs of the Vijayanagara age is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Manucharitra was written by Allasani Peddana.

q.s: Before he seized the Vijayanagara throne in 1485, Saluva Narasimha was the governor of:
q.x: Saluva Narasimha ruled Chandragiri as governor; Penukonda became the capital only after Talikota.

q.s: The Mahanavami Dibba at Hampi, linked with the Mahanavami festival, was built by:
q.x: Krishnadevaraya built the Mahanavami Dibba; the financial year began with the Mahanavami festival.

q.s: The Indian Penal Code, drafted by the First Law Commission under Macaulay, was enacted in:
q.x: The IPC was enacted in 1860; the CPC came in 1859 and the CrPC in 1861.

q.s: In the Battle of Bobbili (1757), Vijayaramaraju of Vizianagaram was helped by the French commander:
q.x: Bussy's French forces helped destroy Bobbili; Ranga Rao of Bobbili died in the battle.

q.s: Who avenged the fall of Bobbili by killing Vijayaramaraju?
q.x: Tandra Papayya, brother-in-law of Ranga Rao, killed Vijayaramaraju soon after the battle.

q.s: Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy, who rebelled against the British in 1846, was publicly hanged in 1847 near:
q.x: He looted the Koilakuntla treasury, was captured at Pairamalla Konda and hanged near Koilakuntla on 22 February 1847.

q.s: The famous patriotic song 'Makoddi Tella Doratanamu' was written by:
q.x: Garimella Satyanarayana wrote it during the Non-Cooperation days; he was jailed for it.

q.s: At a secret meeting in 1934 at Vijayawada, who became secretary of the first committee of the Andhra communists?
q.x: P. Sundarayya became secretary of the seven-member committee formed in 1934; Chandra Rajeswara Rao was secretary at the 1943 open conference.

q.s: Pusumanu Gunnamma, a martyr of the anti-zamindari struggle, was killed in the police firing of 1940 at:
q.x: The Mandasa (Srikakulam) firing of 1 April 1940 killed five people, including Gunnamma.

q.s: The Telugu University, into which the State akademis of Andhra Pradesh were merged, was set up in 1985 by the government of:
q.x: The NTR government created the Telugu University in 1985 and merged the akademis into it.

q.s: The Telugu daily 'Eenadu' was founded in 1974 at Visakhapatnam by:
q.x: Ramoji Rao founded Eenadu; Andhra Jyothi was started by K.L.N. Prasad and Udayam by Dasari Narayana Rao.

q.s: Which of the following Telugu daily–founder pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Sakshi (2008) was founded by Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy.

q.s: Under the Cabinet Mission Plan, the total strength of the Constituent Assembly was fixed at:
q.x: It was 389: 296 from British India (292 provinces + 4 Chief Commissioner's provinces) and 93 from princely states.

q.s: Which one of the following statements about the Constituent Assembly is correct?
o: The representatives of the princely states were nominated by their rulers
Sarojini Naidu was its only woman member
Its members were elected directly by adult franchise
q.x: Princely state members were nominated by rulers; provincial members were elected indirectly by the provincial assemblies; there were about 15 women members.

q.s: Mayurasharman was the founder of which dynasty?
q.x: Mayurasharman founded the Kadamba dynasty with its capital at Vanavasi (Banavasi).

q.s: Which of the following founder–dynasty pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Shrisantamula (Vasishthiputra Chamtamula) founded the Ikshvaku dynasty of Vijayapuri, not the Vishnukundins.

q.s: According to Census 2011, India's sex ratio (females per 1000 males) was:
q.x: The final Census 2011 figure was 943 (the provisional figure was 940).

q.s: According to Census 2011, which State had the lowest sex ratio?
q.x: Haryana had the lowest sex ratio (879) and Kerala the highest (1084).

q.s: Which one of the following statements about population is correct?
o: India's demographic dividend window ends by about 2035
The dependency ratio is the working-age population divided by dependants
India has passed its youth bulge and is in the ageing stage
In the demographic transition, the death rate falls before the birth rate
q.x: The dependency ratio is (0–14 + 65+) ÷ (15–64); India is in its youth-bulge stage with a dividend window to about 2055.

q.s: 'Caste is not merely a division of labour, it is a division of labourers' – who said this?
q.x: Ambedkar wrote this in 'Annihilation of Caste'.

q.s: Which of the following is an ECONOMIC cause of high-risk families?
q.x: Debt and poverty are economic causes; stress and addiction are psychological, social exclusion is social.

q.s: The 'Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat' campaign against child marriage was launched by which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Women and Child Development
q.x: The Ministry of Women and Child Development launched it in 2024.

q.s: The Committee on the Status of Women in India, which gave the report 'Towards Equality' (1974), was chaired by:
q.x: Phulrenu Guha chaired it (constituted 1971); Vina Mazumdar was its Member-Secretary.

q.s: Under the Assisted Reproductive Technology (Regulation) Act, 2021, which of the following is prohibited?
o: Use of ART by married couples
q.x: The Act prohibits the sale of gametes and sex-selective ART.

q.s: Which of the following communal riot–State pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Kokrajhar is in Assam.

q.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, Hyderabad was made the common capital of both States for a period not exceeding:
q.x: Section 5 made Hyderabad the common capital for up to 10 years (till 2 June 2024).

q.s: The special backward-areas package under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 covers how many districts of residuary Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: It covers 7 districts — 4 of Rayalaseema and 3 of North Andhra — at ₹50 crore per district per year.

q.s: Under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, the burden of proving that no offence was committed lies on:
q.x: Section 8A places the burden of proof on the accused.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT included in the definition of 'dowry' under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961?
o: Property given in connection with the marriage
Valuable security demanded as a condition of marriage
Money given by the bride's parents to the groom's family for the marriage
q.x: Mahr under Muslim personal law is excluded; demanding dowry is punishable with six months to two years.

q.s: The Jaya Jaitly Task Force (2020) recommended raising the minimum age of marriage for women from 18 to:
q.x: It recommended raising the age to 21, the same as men.

q.s: Which of the following committee–subject pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Phulrenu Guha Committee – Status of women
Justice J.S. Verma Committee – Crimes against women
Jaya Jaitly Task Force – Marriage age of women
q.x: The Gurupadaswamy Committee (1979) dealt with child labour.

q.s: Which one of the following statements about gender budgeting in India is correct?
o: Gender Budgeting Cells were mandated by the Ministry of Women and Child Development
It is presented as a separate budget outside the Union Budget
The Gender Budget Statement is part of the Union Budget documents
q.x: The Gender Budget Statement has been part of the Union Budget since 2005-06; the Ministry of Finance mandated the cells in 2004-05.

q.s: Under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, a petition to annul a child marriage can be filed by the party who was a minor within:
q.x: A child marriage is voidable; the petition must be filed within two years of attaining majority.

q.s: The Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana, a pension scheme for senior citizens, is operated by:
q.x: PMVVY is run by LIC under the Ministry of Finance; its purchase limit was raised to ₹15 lakh in 2018.

q.s: The National Health Mission has which two sub-missions?
q.x: NHM comprises the National Rural Health Mission and the National Urban Health Mission; ASHAs and ANMs are its backbone.

q.s: The Village and Ward Secretariat system for doorstep delivery of services was introduced in Andhra Pradesh in:
q.x: Village and Ward Secretariats began in October 2019; e-Seva dates from 2001.

q.s: Which of the following Andhra Pradesh e-governance initiative–year pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: APSWAN, the Secretariat–district network, dates from 1998–99.

q.s: Under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Rules, 1995, the State-level Vigilance and Monitoring Committee is headed by the:
q.x: The State committee is chaired by the Chief Minister; the District committee by the District Magistrate.

q.s: Under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, a 'benchmark disability' means a specified disability of not less than:
q.x: A benchmark disability is at least 40% of a specified disability.

q.s: Under the RPwD Act, 2016, the reservation in government jobs for persons with benchmark disabilities is:
q.x: 4% of vacancies in every group of posts; 5% seats are reserved in government and aided higher education institutions.

q.s: The violent clash between Indian and Chinese troops on 15 June 2020 took place in which area?
q.x: The Galwan clash in eastern Ladakh took place in June 2020; Depsang was 2013 and Yangtse 2022.

q.s: The Sumdorong Chu standoff of 1986–87 between India and China took place in which present State?
q.x: Sumdorong Chu is in the Tawang district of Arunachal Pradesh.

q.s: The invitation to the leaders of SAARC countries to the Prime Minister's swearing-in in May 2014 reflected which policy?
q.x: Neighbourhood First gives priority to India's immediate South Asian neighbours.

q.s: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the G4 group seeking permanent seats in the UN Security Council?
q.x: G4 is Brazil, Germany, India and Japan; Italy leads the 'Uniting for Consensus' group that opposes new permanent seats.

q.s: The Secretariat of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) is located at:
q.x: The ASEAN Secretariat is at Jakarta; ASEAN was founded by the Bangkok Declaration of 8 August 1967.

q.s: Which is the only ASEAN member country sharing a land border with India?
q.x: Myanmar is the only ASEAN country bordering India.

q.s: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP)?
q.x: India opted out in 2019; RCEP was signed on 15 November 2020 and covers about 30% of the world's population.

q.s: Which Central Armed Police Force guards India's borders with Nepal and Bhutan?
q.x: The SSB, the newest border force, guards the Nepal and Bhutan borders.

q.s: Which of the following forces does NOT guard any of India's international land borders?
q.x: The CRPF (1939, as the Crown Representative's Police) handles internal security; BSF, ITBP, SSB and Assam Rifles are border guarding forces.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution bars discussion in Parliament on the conduct of a Supreme Court or High Court judge, except on a motion for removal?
q.x: Article 121 imposes the restriction; Article 122 bars courts from inquiring into parliamentary proceedings.

q.s: The power of the Supreme Court to pass any order necessary for 'complete justice' is provided under:
q.x: Article 142 gives the power to do complete justice; Article 141 makes its law binding on all courts.

q.s: Which of the following Union–State Article pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Summoning of the House: Art. 85 – Art. 174
q.x: Collective responsibility in States is Art. 164(2); Art. 163 deals with the Council of Ministers aiding the Governor.

q.s: Who was the first Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Fort William, set up under the Regulating Act in 1774?
q.x: Sir Elijah Impey was the first Chief Justice; Macaulay was the first Law Member of the Governor-General's Council (1834).

q.s: Who was the first Law Member of the Governor-General's Council under the Charter Act of 1833?
q.x: Thomas Babington Macaulay became the first Law Member in 1834.

q.s: In which offer did the British first accept that framing a new constitution was primarily the responsibility of Indians?
q.x: The August Offer (1940) of Linlithgow accepted the principle; the Cripps Mission (1942) proposed an elected constitution-making body.

q.s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar warned against the 'grammar of anarchy' in his closing speech to the Constituent Assembly delivered on:
q.x: He gave the speech on 25 November 1949, a day before the Constitution was adopted.

q.s: The concept of judicial review in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the Constitution of:
q.x: Judicial review comes from the USA (Marbury v. Madison, 1803); Britain follows parliamentary sovereignty.

q.s: Which of the following rights is NOT available to an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) Cardholder?
o: Right to vote in Lok Sabha elections
Exemption from registering with police for any length of stay
Parity with NRIs in certain economic matters
q.x: OCI Cardholders, registered under Section 7A of the Citizenship Act, have no voting rights.

q.s: Which one of the following statements about Overseas Citizens of India is correct?
o: An OCI Cardholder can vote in Lok Sabha elections
An OCI Cardholder is registered under Section 7A of the Citizenship Act, 1955
An OCI Cardholder is a citizen of India
An OCI Cardholder needs a fresh visa for every visit
q.x: OCI is registration, not citizenship; it gives a lifelong multiple-entry visa but no voting rights.

q.s: The first National Emergency, proclaimed on 26 October 1962 on Chinese aggression, was declared by President:
q.x: President S. Radhakrishnan proclaimed it; the 1971 Emergency came under V.V. Giri.

q.s: The Emergency of 25 June 1975 on the ground of 'internal disturbance' was proclaimed by President:
q.x: Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed proclaimed it after the Allahabad High Court voided Indira Gandhi's election on 12 June 1975.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that the majority of a ministry must be tested on the floor of the House, not by the Governor's opinion?
q.x: The nine-judge bench in S.R. Bommai (1994) also held secularism and federalism to be basic features.

q.s: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution secures to all citizens liberty of:
o: Thought, expression, belief, faith and worship
q.x: The Preamble lists liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship; equality of status and opportunity is a separate ideal.

q.s: The 'rarest of rare' doctrine for awarding the death penalty was laid down by the Supreme Court in:
q.x: Bachan Singh v State of Punjab (1980) limited the death penalty to the rarest of rare cases.

q.s: The judgment in State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (1951) led to the insertion of:
q.x: The Court struck down the communal G.O.; the First Amendment (1951) added Article 15(4).

q.s: In the Indra Sawhney case (1992), the Supreme Court fixed the ceiling on total reservations at:
q.x: It upheld 27% OBC reservation, excluded the OBC creamy layer and upheld a 50% ceiling.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT held by the Supreme Court in the Indra Sawhney case (1992)?
o: The creamy layer among OBCs must be excluded
Total reservation should not normally exceed 50%
q.x: Indra Sawhney held that reservation does not extend to promotions; the 77th Amendment (1995) later inserted Article 16(4A).

q.s: Article 15(5), enabling reservation in admission to private unaided educational institutions, was inserted by the:
q.x: The 93rd Amendment (2005) inserted Article 15(5); minority institutions under Article 30(1) are excluded.

q.s: An amendment on which of the following does NOT require ratification by half of the State Legislatures?
o: Any List of the Seventh Schedule
q.x: Fundamental Rights can be amended by a special majority of Parliament alone; the other three are federal provisions needing State ratification.

q.s: Clauses (4) and (5) of Article 368, inserted by the 42nd Amendment to bar judicial review of amendments, were struck down in:
q.x: Minerva Mills (1980) held that a limited amending power is itself a basic feature.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that the High Courts' powers of judicial review under Articles 226 and 227 are part of the basic structure?
q.x: L. Chandra Kumar (1997) held that tribunal decisions remain subject to High Court review under Articles 226 and 227.

q.s: Which one of the following statements is correct?
o: The Indian Parliament is sovereign in the British sense
The amending power of Parliament under Article 368 is unlimited
Laws and amendments made by the Indian Parliament are subject to judicial review
Courts in Britain can strike down Acts of Parliament
q.x: India has a written, supreme Constitution and judicial review, so its Parliament is not sovereign like Britain's; the amending power is limited by the basic structure.

q.s: The 'appointed day' on which the State of Telangana was formed under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 was:
q.x: The appointed day was 2 June 2014; the Act was made under Articles 3 and 4.

q.s: Who was the first to be recognised as the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, in 1969?
q.x: Ram Subhag Singh of the Congress (O) was recognised in 1969; the LoP's office is statutory (1977 Act).

q.s: To be recognised as the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, the largest opposition party must hold at least what share of the total strength of the House?
q.x: The convention requires at least one-tenth of the House strength (the quorum).

q.s: Which of the following Finance Commission–Chairman pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The 13th FC was chaired by Vijay Kelkar; Y.V. Reddy chaired the 14th.

q.s: Who was the first Chairman of the Finance Commission (1951)?
q.x: K.C. Neogy chaired the First Finance Commission.

q.s: Which of the following 'first holder' pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: First Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog – Rajiv Kumar
First Chairperson of the NHRC – Justice Ranganath Misra
First Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission – Gulzarilal Nanda
First Chairman of the Finance Commission – K.C. Neogy
q.x: Arvind Panagariya was NITI Aayog's first Vice-Chairman; Rajiv Kumar was the second.

q.s: The Inter-State Council, set up by a Presidential order in 1990 on the Sarkaria Commission's advice, is provided for under:
q.x: Article 263 provides for an Inter-State Council.

q.s: Which one of the following statements about the UN Human Rights Council is correct?
o: Its members are elected by the UN General Assembly for three-year terms
Its members are elected by the UN Security Council
A member can serve any number of consecutive terms
It is based in New York
q.x: The 47-member Council (Geneva, 2006) is elected by the UNGA; members may serve at most two consecutive terms and can be suspended by a two-thirds UNGA vote.

q.s: Proactive disclosure of information by public authorities is provided under which Section of the RTI Act, 2005?
q.x: Section 4 deals with proactive disclosure; Section 8 with exemptions and Section 19 with appeals.

q.s: Which of the following RTI Act provisions is NOT correctly matched?
o: Section 19 – Complaints to the Information Commission
q.x: Section 19 deals with appeals; complaints are under Section 18.

q.s: The setting up of a Lokpal and Lokayuktas was first recommended by the:
q.x: The First ARC (1966) recommended them; the first Lokpal Bill was introduced in 1968.

q.s: During a National Emergency, the President can modify the distribution of revenues between the Centre and the States under:
q.x: Article 354 allows changes up to the end of the financial year; Article 353 lets the Union direct the States on any matter.

q.s: Which of the following Articles is NOT an emergency provision of the Constitution?
q.x: Article 368 deals with amendment; 352 (national), 356 (State) and 360 (financial) are emergency provisions.

q.s: Which one of the following statements about the North Eastern Council is correct?
o: It is a statutory body set up under the North Eastern Council Act, 1971
It is a constitutional body under Article 263
It was set up under the Sixth Schedule
q.x: The NEC is statutory; Sikkim became its eighth member in 2002.

q.s: A new All India Service can be created if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution supported by:
o: A simple majority of members present
Two-thirds of members present and voting
Three-fourths of members present and voting
q.x: Article 312 requires a Rajya Sabha resolution backed by two-thirds of members present and voting.

q.s: After the 1989 Lok Sabha elections, in which the Congress was the largest party, the government was formed by the:
q.x: The National Front under V.P. Singh formed the government; the Congress, with 197 seats, sat in opposition.

q.s: Under the Election Commission's cVIGIL app, action on a reported violation of the Model Code of Conduct is promised within:
q.x: cVIGIL takes geo-tagged complaints and promises action within 100 minutes.

q.s: The District Planning Committee is provided for under which Article of the Constitution?
q.x: Article 243ZD provides for the DPC; Article 243ZE for the Metropolitan Planning Committee.

q.s: Which one of the following statements about the 74th Constitutional Amendment is correct?
o: It came into force on 24 April 1993
Municipalities are handled by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj
q.x: Part IXA spans Arts. 243P–243ZG; the Twelfth Schedule has 18 subjects; the 74th came into force on 1 June 1993 (24 April 1993 is the 73rd's date); municipalities are with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

q.s: The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 (PESA) applies to:
q.x: PESA extends Part IX to Fifth Schedule areas; Sixth Schedule areas have Autonomous District Councils.

q.s: Which of the following States does NOT have tribal areas under the Sixth Schedule?
q.x: The Sixth Schedule covers Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram; Manipur's hill councils are under a separate Act.

q.s: Who described Indian village communities as 'Little Republics'?
q.x: Sir Charles Metcalfe called them 'little republics'.

q.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1919, local self-government was made a:
q.x: Local self-government became a transferred subject under dyarchy; the 1935 Act made it a provincial subject.

q.s: Trading under India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme is regulated by the:
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India
q.x: CERC regulates trading; the Bureau of Energy Efficiency is the administrator of the scheme.

q.s: Under the Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM) for highway projects, the government pays what share of the project cost during construction?
q.x: Under HAM the government pays 40% during construction and the rest as annuities.

q.s: Which of the following highway project models is NOT a public-private partnership model?
q.x: Under EPC the Government funds the whole project and the private party only builds it.

q.s: e-Kranti, the National e-Governance Plan 2.0 approved in 2015, includes how many Mission Mode Projects?
q.x: e-Kranti has 44 MMPs (15 Central, 17 State, 12 Integrated); its vision is 'Transforming e-Governance for Transforming Governance'.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, 'e-Pragati' refers to:
o: A data network linking the Secretariat with districts
q.x: e-Pragati is the state enterprise architecture; APSWAN is the network, eSeva the citizen centres and e-Procurement online tendering.

q.s: In 'MUDRA', the 'R' stands for:
q.x: MUDRA is the Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency; PMMY loans go to non-corporate, non-farm micro enterprises.

q.s: The 'Spandana' grievance system launched in Andhra Pradesh in 2019 has been replaced by:
q.x: Spandana was succeeded by the AI-based Public Grievance Redressal System (PGRS).

q.s: India continued as a full member of the Commonwealth even after becoming a republic, under the:
q.x: The London Declaration (1949) let republics stay in the Commonwealth, accepting the Crown only as its Head.

q.s: India hosted the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) at New Delhi in:
q.x: CHOGM was held at New Delhi in 1983.

q.s: Which airport became the world's first fully solar-powered airport in 2015?
q.x: Cochin, also India's first PPP airport, went fully solar in 2015.

q.s: India's first deep-water transhipment port, Vizhinjam, is located in:
q.x: Vizhinjam is near Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala.

q.s: Under the three-capitals proposal of 2020 for Andhra Pradesh, which city was to be the judicial capital?
q.x: Kurnool was to be judicial, Visakhapatnam executive and Amaravati legislative capital.

q.s: The foundation stone of Amaravati, the capital of Andhra Pradesh, was laid by PM Narendra Modi on 22 October 2015 at:
q.x: It was laid at Uddandarayunipalem; 'Restart Amaravati' followed on 2 May 2025.

q.s: Which one of the following statements about welfare 'firsts' in India is correct?
o: The National Social Assistance Programme was launched in 1995
India's first National Population Policy came in 2000
The Etawah Pilot Project was India's first poverty alleviation programme
The National Nutrition Policy came before the first Population Policy
q.x: NSAP began in 1995; the first Population Policy was of 1976 and the Nutrition Policy of 1993; Etawah was a rural development pilot.

q.s: Under DAY-NRLM, the federation of Self Help Groups formed at the village level is called the:
q.x: The order is SHG, Village Organisation, Cluster-Level Federation; the poor are identified by Participatory Identification of Poor (PIP).

q.s: The Rajiv Gandhi Shilpi Swasthya Bima Yojana provides health insurance to:
q.x: It covers handicraft artisans (Ministry of Textiles); the Mahatma Gandhi Bunkar Bima Yojana gives life cover to handloom weavers.

q.s: The Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission, launched in February 2016, aims to develop how many Rurban clusters?
q.x: SPMRM targets 300 clusters; it was launched at Kurubhat (Rajnandgaon, Chhattisgarh).

q.s: The concept of PURA (Providing Urban Amenities in Rural Areas), a forerunner of the Rurban Mission, was put forward by:
q.x: Dr. Kalam explained PURA on the eve of Republic Day 2003.

q.s: Under the Smart Cities Mission, the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) for each city is a company incorporated under the:
o: Municipal Corporations Act of the State
q.x: Each SPV is a Companies Act, 2013 company with 50:50 equity of the State/UT and the ULB.

q.s: The Economic Survey 2025-26 calls for a shift in the role of the State from 'regulation and control' to:
q.x: The Survey favours an enabling State with trust-based compliance rather than inspection-based enforcement.

q.s: The hypothesis that female labour force participation first falls with early income growth and later rises with education and service jobs is known as the:
q.x: This is the U-shaped hypothesis of female LFPR; the inverted U is Kuznets's inequality curve.

q.s: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956, called India's 'Economic Constitution', reserved how many industries in Schedule A exclusively for the State?
q.x: Schedule A had 17 industries and Schedule B 12; the 1991 policy cut the reserved list from 17 to 8.

q.s: The Industrial Finance Corporation of India (IFCI) was set up in:
q.x: IFCI was set up in 1948, the year of the first Industrial Policy Resolution.

q.s: According to the Environmental Kuznets Curve, the relationship between per capita income and environmental degradation takes the shape of:
q.x: Degradation first rises with income and then falls after a turning point, giving an inverted U.

q.s: The inverted-U hypothesis linking economic growth and income inequality (1955) was put forward by:
q.x: Simon Kuznets proposed it; Lorenz gave the Lorenz curve (1905) and Gini the Gini coefficient (1912).

q.s: Unemployment caused by rapid population growth, labour immobility and a shift to capital-intensive production is described as:
q.x: These long-run causes make Indian unemployment structural in nature.

q.s: Which Five Year Plan shifted the emphasis of development from heavy industry to infrastructure?
q.x: The Eighth Plan (1992–97), the first after the reforms, shifted emphasis to infrastructure.

q.s: Under the New Industrial Policy of 1991, automatic approval was given to foreign direct investment in high-priority industries up to:
q.x: Automatic approval was given up to 51%; other proposals went to the FIPB.

q.s: The Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) was set up to:
q.x: BIFR dealt with the revival of sick industrial companies.

q.s: Which of the following sectors remained largely a state monopoly after the 1991 reforms?
q.x: Railways stayed largely with the State, while telecom, civil aviation and banking opened to private players.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Finance Commission under Article 280?
o: Distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the States
Principles governing grants-in-aid to States under Article 275
Maintaining the accounts of the Union and the States
Measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State for local bodies
q.x: Accounts are the work of the CAG; the other three are Finance Commission functions. GST sharing is settled by the GST Council.

q.s: The SVAMITVA scheme, which uses drones to map rural inhabited land, is implemented by the:
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
q.x: SVAMITVA is a scheme of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj (with Survey of India as technology partner).

q.s: The 17 Sustainable Development Goals adopted by the UN in September 2015 have how many targets?
q.x: The SDGs have 169 targets under the 2030 Agenda; they are not legally binding.

q.s: India's National Indicator Framework for monitoring the SDGs is prepared by:
o: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
q.x: MoSPI frames the NIF; NITI Aayog prepares the SDG India Index.

q.s: Bank deposits remaining unclaimed for 10 years or more are transferred to the:
o: Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation
q.x: Under Section 26A of the Banking Regulation Act, they go to the RBI's DEA Fund.

q.s: The Market Stabilisation Scheme introduced by the RBI in April 2004 was meant to:
o: Sterilise excess liquidity created by foreign-exchange inflows
q.x: MSS bonds absorbed liquidity from the RBI's forex purchases; OMOs manage durable liquidity and the LAF day-to-day liquidity.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a quantitative instrument of monetary policy?
q.x: Moral suasion is a qualitative (selective) tool.

q.s: The Monetary Policy Committee was given a statutory basis by the RBI (Amendment) Act, 2016 under which Section of the RBI Act, 1934?
q.x: Section 45ZB provides for the MPC and Section 45ZA for the inflation target; the 2015 MPFA itself was only an agreement.

q.s: Which one of the following statements about flexible inflation targeting is correct?
o: Section 45ZA of the RBI Act deals with the MPC
The MPFA is a law passed by Parliament
The Monetary Policy Framework Agreement of 2015 is an agreement, not a statute
The MPC was created by the RBI Act of 1934 itself
q.x: The MPFA (20 February 2015) is a Government–RBI agreement; the 2016 amendment inserted Sections 45Z–45ZO (45ZA inflation target, 45ZB MPC).

q.s: India Post Payments Bank began its operations in:
q.x: IPPB was launched in September 2018 (licence in 2015); India Post is the world's largest postal network.

q.s: Which of the following banks was NOT nationalised in 1969?
q.x: Andhra Bank was nationalised in the second batch of 1980, along with Vijaya Bank, Corporation Bank and Oriental Bank of Commerce.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT among the Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs) identified by the RBI?
q.x: The RBI's D-SIBs are SBI, ICICI Bank and HDFC Bank.

q.s: Global Systemically Important Banks (G-SIBs) are identified by the:
o: Bank for International Settlements Board of Directors
q.x: The FSB, with the Basel Committee, publishes the G-SIB list; no Indian bank is on it.

q.s: Under the new income-tax regime, the rebate that makes income up to ₹12 lakh tax-free is given under Section:
q.x: The rebate is under Section 87A; Section 115BAC sets out the default new regime.

q.s: Which one of the following statements about GST 2.0 is correct?
o: It came into effect on 22 September 2025
It retained the 28% slab for luxury goods
GST rates can be changed only by amending the GST Acts
The statutory ceiling for CGST is 40%
q.x: GST 2.0 began on 22 September 2025, replacing the 28% slab with a 40% rate for sin/ultra-luxury goods; rates change by notification on the Council's advice; the CGST ceiling is 20%.

q.s: A decision of the GST Council requires a majority of not less than what share of the weighted votes of members present and voting?
q.x: Decisions need three-fourths of weighted votes; the Centre has one-third and all States together two-thirds.

q.s: In the GST Council, the vote of the Central Government carries a weight of:
o: One-half of the total votes cast
One-fourth of the total votes cast
Two-thirds of the total votes cast
One-third of the total votes cast
q.x: The Centre's vote is one-third; the quorum is one-half of total members.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?
o: Salary of the Comptroller and Auditor General
q.x: Ministers' salaries are voted; the CAG's, President's and Supreme Court judges' emoluments are charged and not put to vote (Art. 112(3)).

q.s: The Special Economic Zones Act, offering a simplified and business-friendly regime for export production, was enacted in:
q.x: The SEZ Act was passed in 2005 and came into force in 2006.

q.s: The FDI cap in the insurance sector was raised to 74 per cent with effect from:
q.x: It went from 26% to 49% in 2015 and to 74% from 19 May 2021; insurance is Entry 47 of the Union List.

q.s: Which of the following crops is NOT expanding in area in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Ragi and jowar are shrinking; maize (for poultry feed), oil palm, horticulture and aquaculture are expanding.

q.s: India's average rice yield (about 2,900 kg/ha) is less than half that of:
q.x: China's rice yield is about 7,100 kg/ha, far above India's.

q.s: Glyricidia, widely planted on farm bunds, is mainly used as:
q.x: Glyricidia is a leguminous tree whose loppings are used as green leaf manure.

q.s: Which one of the following statements about the farm laws of 2020 is correct?
o: They imposed permanent stock limits on all foodgrains
They were enacted under the Union List
They were repealed by Parliament in November 2021
q.x: They rested on Concurrent List Entry 33; the Supreme Court stayed them in January 2021 and Parliament repealed them in November 2021.

q.s: According to the Shanta Kumar High-Level Committee, about what share of farmers sell their produce at MSP?
q.x: The Committee estimated that only about 6% of farmers sell at MSP.

q.s: The Agricultural Prices Commission was renamed the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) in:
q.x: The APC (1965) became the CACP in 1985.

q.s: Which one of the following statements about the CACP is correct?
o: It is a statutory body set up under an Act of Parliament
It is an attached office of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Its MSP recommendations are binding on the Government
It was set up on the advice of the Shanta Kumar Committee
q.x: The CACP is an attached office, not a statutory body; the Government takes the final decision on MSP.

q.s: Under the New Public Sector Enterprise Policy, 2021, PSEs in non-strategic sectors are to be:
q.x: Non-strategic PSEs are to be privatised or closed; in strategic sectors only a bare minimum presence is kept.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the strategic sectors under the New Public Sector Enterprise Policy, 2021?
q.x: The four strategic groups include transport and telecom besides the three listed; tourism is non-strategic.

q.s: The reservation of items for exclusive manufacture in the small-scale sector, begun in 1967, was fully removed in:
q.x: The last items were de-reserved in 2015.

q.s: Which of the following ports in Andhra Pradesh was developed under public-private partnership?
q.x: Gangavaram and Krishnapatnam are PPP ports; Visakhapatnam is a major port under the Union.

q.s: Which State gets about 64 per cent of its Gross State Value Added (GSVA) from services?
q.x: Kerala's services share is about 64.3%; among UTs Chandigarh leads at 88.8%.

q.s: The 16th Finance Commission gives what weight to the 'income distance' criterion in horizontal devolution?
q.x: Income distance carries 42.5% under the 16th FC (45% under the 15th); it reduces the share of higher-income States like AP.

q.s: The Polavaram irrigation project was declared a national project under which Section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
q.x: Section 90 declared Polavaram on the Godavari a national project; the AP Government executes it for the Centre.

q.s: Among Kharif crops, the highest Minimum Support Price per quintal for 2026-27 is for:
q.x: Sesamum has the highest Kharif MSP (₹10,346 per quintal).

q.s: The first Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal (KWDT-I), which gave its award in 1976, was headed by:
q.x: KWDT-I under R.S. Bachawat distributed 2,130 TMC at 75% dependability; KWDT-II was headed by Brijesh Kumar.

q.s: How much water did KWDT-I allocate to combined Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Combined Andhra Pradesh got 811 TMC; Maharashtra got 560 TMC and Karnataka 700 TMC.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, large industrial investment proposals are cleared by the 'SIPB', which stands for:
q.x: The State Investment Promotion Board, chaired by the Chief Minister, clears projects that the Cabinet then ratifies.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh's Industrial Development Policy (4.0), along with the MSME, Electronics and Food Processing policies, was notified on:
q.x: The 4.0 suite was notified on 26 October 2024 (G.O.s 68 to 71).

q.s: Under the Thirteenth Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, the feasibility of a SAIL steel plant was to be examined in which district?
q.x: The steel plant in YSR (Kadapa) district is only to be 'examined'; only the new major port 'shall' be developed.

q.s: The new major port promised under the Thirteenth Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act was proposed at:
q.x: Dugarajapatnam (Nellore) was named; the site was later shifted to Ramayapatnam.

q.s: Under the UDAY scheme (2015) for power distribution companies, 75 per cent of DISCOM debt was taken over by the:
q.x: States took over 75% of DISCOM debt over 2015-16 and 2016-17.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh was reorganised from 13 into 26 districts in:
q.x: The 26-district reorganisation took effect in April 2022.

q.s: After the 2025 re-measurement, Andhra Pradesh's coastline (about 1,053 km) ranks where among Indian States?
q.x: It is the third longest, after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.

q.s: The Earth is nearest to the Sun (perihelion) in the month of:
q.x: The orbit is elliptical: perihelion is in early January and aphelion in early July.

q.s: Which one of the following statements about the Earth's revolution is correct?
o: The Earth–Sun distance is constant throughout the year
The Earth is farthest from the Sun in January
The Earth–Sun distance varies because the orbit is elliptical
q.x: The orbit is elliptical: perihelion in January, aphelion in July; one revolution takes about 365¼ days.

q.s: Because of the Earth's rotation, the Coriolis force deflects winds in the Northern Hemisphere:
q.x: The Coriolis force deflects moving air to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern.

q.s: India's only active volcano is located at:
q.x: Barren Island in the Andaman Sea is active; Narcondam is dormant and Baratang has mud volcanoes.

q.s: Mud volcanoes in India are found at:
q.x: Baratang in Middle Andaman has mud volcanoes; Dhinodhar in Kutch is an extinct volcanic hill.

q.s: The Chambal ravines are a classic example of which type of erosion?
q.x: Running water cutting deep channels produced the Chambal ravines (gully erosion).

q.s: Which type of soil particle holds the maximum water?
q.x: Clay holds the most water because of its very small pores and large surface area.

q.s: Which of the following countries does NOT border the Caspian Sea?
q.x: Uzbekistan is doubly landlocked; the Caspian states are Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan.

q.s: At the onset of an El Nino event, the easterly trade winds over the equatorial Pacific:
q.x: Weaker trade winds deepen the thermocline off Peru, weaken the cold upwelling and warm the sea there.

q.s: The Long Period Average (LPA) of India's southwest monsoon rainfall used by the IMD is about:
q.x: The LPA (1971–2020) is about 87 cm; a forecast of 92% of LPA is 'below normal'.

q.s: The term 'Modoki' in 'El Nino Modoki' is a Japanese word meaning:
q.x: Modoki means 'similar but different'; El Nino is Spanish for 'the little boy' (Christ child) and La Nina 'the little girl'.

q.s: Which of the following lowers the salinity of sea water?
q.x: Melting ice and river inflow lower salinity (as in the Black Sea); freezing and evaporation raise it.

q.s: The Northern Circars coastal plain extends between:
q.x: The Northern Circars run from the Mahanadi to the Krishna; Konkan is Daman–Goa and Malabar Mangaluru–Kanyakumari.

q.s: The Ghaghara, a left-bank tributary of the Ganga, rises at the:
q.x: The Ghaghara rises at the Mapchachungo glacier south of Mansarovar.

q.s: The Kalagarh Dam in Uttarakhand is built on the river:
q.x: Kalagarh Dam is on the Ramganga.

q.s: The Rechna Doab of the Punjab lies between which two rivers?
q.x: Rechna is Ravi–Chenab; Bist is Beas–Sutlej and Chaj is Chenab–Jhelum.

q.s: The Krishna river, which flows east to the Bay of Bengal, rises at:
q.x: It rises at Mahabaleshwar in the Western Ghats, about 64 km from the Arabian Sea, and flows east as the Deccan slopes eastward.

q.s: Which of the following rivers does NOT rise at Amarkantak?
q.x: The Damodar rises in the Chota Nagpur plateau of Jharkhand; the Narmada, Son and Johila rise at Amarkantak.

q.s: The Gosthani river of north coastal Andhra Pradesh rises in the Anantagiri hills and meets the sea near:
q.x: The Gosthani has its estuary near Bheemunipatnam.

q.s: The Tungabhadra river is formed by the union of:
q.x: Tunga and Bhadra join to form the Tungabhadra; Veda and Avathi form the Vedavathi.

q.s: Which river has the longest course within the present State of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: The Penna flows about 536 km inside AP; the Godavari is the longest river flowing through the State overall.

q.s: In a soil profile, the horizon in which minerals washed down from the upper layers accumulate is the:
q.x: The B horizon (subsoil) is the zone of accumulation; the order from the top is O, A, B, C, R.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, topsoil loss caused by Podu (shifting) cultivation is a serious problem mainly in:
o: Alluri Sitharama Raju and Parvathipuram Manyam
q.x: Podu is practised in the tribal hill districts; Anantapur faces desertification and the deltas salinity and waterlogging.

q.s: Red sanders (Pterocarpus santalinus) is endemic to which forest region of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Red sanders grows in the dry deciduous forests of the southern Eastern Ghats, notably the Seshachalam hills.

q.s: Which category forms the largest share (about 85.8 per cent) of the notified forest area of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Reserved Forests form about 85.8%, Protected Forests about 13.6% and Unclassed Forests about 0.6%.

q.s: The Southern Campus of the National Institute of Disaster Management (NIDM) is located at:
q.x: The NIDM Southern Campus is at Kondapalli (NTR district) in Andhra Pradesh.

q.s: Which of the following historic disaster–country pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Crete is in Greece.

q.s: Why is the east coast of India hit by cyclones far more often than the west coast?
o: The Bay of Bengal generates about four times as many cyclones as the Arabian Sea
The east coast has more mountains
The Arabian Sea is warmer than the Bay of Bengal
The Western Ghats attract cyclones away
q.x: The Bay of Bengal to Arabian Sea ratio of cyclones is about 4:1.

q.s: The lignite deposits of Neyveli in Tamil Nadu belong to the:
q.x: Neyveli lignite is Tertiary; Gondwana coal of the Damodar, Son, Mahanadi and Godavari valleys is older.

q.s: The Cuddapah basin of Andhra Pradesh is especially known for India's largest deposits of:
q.x: The Proterozoic Cuddapah basin holds barytes (Mangampet), asbestos, steatite, limestone and uranium.

q.s: India aims to raise the share of natural gas in its primary energy mix by 2030 to:
q.x: The target is 15% by 2030 (from about 6%).

q.s: The Ravva oil and gas field in the Krishna–Godavari basin was discovered in 1987 by:
q.x: ONGC discovered Ravva; Cairn later operated it.

q.s: The Sipat Super Thermal Power Station of NTPC is located in which State?
q.x: Sipat is in Bilaspur district, Chhattisgarh; Mundra is in Kutch, Gujarat.

q.s: Which of the following thermal power station–State pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: NTPC Dadri is in Gautam Buddh Nagar, Uttar Pradesh.

q.s: Which of the following States is NOT covered under the 'Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India' (BGREI) programme?
q.x: BGREI (2010-11, under RKVY) targets the rice-based systems of the eastern States, not Punjab.

q.s: The Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC) is being developed with the support of:
q.x: VCIC is backed by the ADB; DMIC is supported by Japan.

q.s: How many industrial corridors are being developed under the National Industrial Corridor Development Programme?
q.x: There are 11 corridors under NICDC (formerly DMICDC, 2008); 12 new industrial smart cities were approved in August 2024.

q.s: The aluminium plant of BALCO is located at:
q.x: BALCO is at Korba, Chhattisgarh; Hindalco is at Renukoot and INDAL had units at Muri (Jharkhand), Hirakud and Alupuram.

q.s: The INDAL aluminium unit at Muri is in which State?
q.x: Muri is in Jharkhand.

q.s: The Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) functions under the:
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
q.x: STPI (1991) is a society under MeitY.

q.s: Udyam registration for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises began on:
q.x: Udyam registration replaced Udyog Aadhaar from 1 July 2020.

q.s: The HBJ gas pipeline, which supplies gas to fertiliser plants such as Sawai Madhopur and Aonla, runs from:
q.x: HBJ is Hazira–Bijaipur–Jagdishpur; pipelines are the cheapest mode for oil and gas.

q.s: Which one of the following statements about pipelines in India is correct?
o: Pipelines are the cheapest mode for transporting oil and gas
The PM Urja Ganga pipeline brings gas from Iran
The HBJ pipeline supplies the Ramagundam fertiliser plant
Pipelines are unsuitable for natural gas
q.x: PM Urja Ganga (JHBDPL) is a domestic eastern pipeline; Ramagundam is not on the HBJ pipeline.

q.s: Which major port of India has overtaken Deendayal (Kandla) as the largest in cargo handling?
q.x: Paradip is now the top cargo-handling major port; JNPA is the largest container port.

q.s: Which is the largest privately owned port in India?
q.x: Mundra in Gujarat (Adani) is the largest private port.

q.s: Which is the oldest artificial port on the east coast of India?
q.x: Chennai's artificial harbour dates from 1881, as the straight coast offered no natural shelter; Visakhapatnam is the deepest landlocked port.

q.s: The Trans-Canadian railway connects Halifax in the east with which city in the west?
q.x: It runs about 7,050 km from Halifax to Vancouver.

q.s: The Andhra Pradesh Tourism Development Corporation (APTDC) runs which chain of hotels and resorts?
q.x: APTDC (1976) runs the Haritha hotels; the AP Tourism Authority handles branding and investment promotion.

q.s: Andhra Pradesh's Industrial Development Policy 4.0 (2024–29) targets an investment of:
q.x: It targets ₹30 lakh crore of investment and US$ 40 billion of exports, with 175+ industrial parks across the State.

q.s: Under the 5+3+3+4 structure of the National Education Policy 2020, the Foundational Stage covers children aged:
q.x: Foundational 3–8, Preparatory 8–11, Middle 11–14 and Secondary 14–18 years.

q.s: Which of the following NEP 2020 stage–age group pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Secondary stage covers 14–18 years.

q.s: The Human Development Report of the UNDP was conceived by:
q.x: Mahbub ul Haq launched the HDR in 1990; Amartya Sen co-designed the HDI and won the Nobel Prize in 1998.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a criterion for a Census Town in India?
o: At least 75% of male main workers in non-agricultural work
Density of at least 400 persons per sq km
Having a municipality or notified town committee
q.x: A place with a municipality is a Statutory Town; a Census Town meets the three demographic criteria.

q.s: According to the UN World Urbanization Prospects 2025, the world's most populous city is:
q.x: Jakarta displaced Tokyo, mainly because of a new method of defining cities.

q.s: Under B.S. Guha's racial classification, the Kadar and Irula tribes belong to the:
q.x: Guha placed the Kadar and Irula (and Andamanese) among the Negritos; Munda, Santhal and Chenchu are Proto-Australoid.

q.s: Marang Buru, worshipped at the Parasnath Hills, is the supreme deity of which tribe?
q.x: Marang Buru is the Santhal supreme deity; Kherai puja belongs to the Bodos.

q.s: Kherai puja is the main religious festival of which tribe?
q.x: Kherai is the chief festival of the Bodos of Assam.

q.s: The Chenchu tribe of Andhra Pradesh mainly lives in the:
q.x: The Chenchus, a PVTG, live in the Nallamala forests; the Korku live in Satpura–Melghat.

q.s: Which of the following tribe–habitat pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Karbis live in Karbi Anglong, Assam.

q.s: Which Naga tribe is known as the last head-hunters of India?
q.x: The Konyaks were the last head-hunters; Longpi pottery belongs to the Tangkhul Nagas.

q.s: Living root bridges are a well-known feature of which State?
q.x: They are found in the Khasi and Jaintia hills of Meghalaya.

q.s: The Hangul (Kashmir stag) is found mainly in:
q.x: Dachigam near Srinagar is the home of the Hangul; Kanha is known for the Barasingha.

q.s: The Rollapadu Wildlife Sanctuary in Andhra Pradesh is known for protecting the:
q.x: Rollapadu (Nandyal district) is a grassland sanctuary for the Great Indian Bustard.

q.s: Which of the following Ramsar site–State pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Menar, added in 2025, is in Rajasthan near Udaipur; the other pairs are correct.

q.s: India's first Ramsar site, designated in 1981, is:
q.x: Chilika (Odisha) and Keoladeo were the first, with Chilika listed first in 1981.

q.s: Which is the only Ramsar site of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Kolleru Lake is AP's only Ramsar site.

q.s: In the Milankovitch theory of climate change, 'obliquity' refers to:
o: The shape of the Earth's orbit
The tilt of the Earth's axis
The wobble of the Earth's axis
q.x: Obliquity is axial tilt; eccentricity is the orbit's shape and precession the wobble.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the Milankovitch cycles?
q.x: Milankovitch cycles are orbital: eccentricity, obliquity and precession; volcanic aerosols cause short-term cooling but are not orbital cycles.

q.s: India's Gross Expenditure on R&D (GERD) as a share of GDP is about:
q.x: GERD is about 0.64–0.65% of GDP, far below the 2% target; DRDO is the largest central R&D spender.

q.s: The INSPIRE scheme to attract young talent to science was launched in 2008 by the:
q.x: INSPIRE is a DST flagship; MANAK stands for Million Minds Augmenting National Aspiration and Knowledge.

q.s: 'Oilzapper', a bacterial product used to clean up oil spills, was developed by TERI together with:
q.x: TERI and Indian Oil developed Oilzapper and Oilivorous-S.

q.s: The Nano Mission, launched in 2007 as an umbrella programme, is run by the:
q.x: The Nano Mission is a DST programme.

q.s: The term 'Fourth Industrial Revolution' was popularised in 2016 by:
q.x: Klaus Schwab of the World Economic Forum popularised it; Alvin Toffler wrote 'The Third Wave'.

q.s: Wi-Fi 7 is based on which IEEE standard?
q.x: Wi-Fi 7 is IEEE 802.11be with Multi-Link Operation; 802.11ax is Wi-Fi 6.

q.s: The Bharat 6G Alliance was launched in:
q.x: It was launched in 2023; 6G networks are expected in the early 2030s.

q.s: 'Agnilet', the world's first single-piece 3D-printed semi-cryogenic rocket engine, was developed by:
q.x: Agnikul Cosmos of Chennai built Agnilet; Skyroot of Hyderabad builds the Vikram rockets.

q.s: 'New Shepard', the reusable suborbital rocket that landed vertically in November 2015, was developed by:
q.x: Blue Origin developed New Shepard; SpaceX's Falcon 9 first stage landed in December 2015.

q.s: Which launch vehicle is being human-rated to carry the Gaganyaan crew?
q.x: The human-rated LVM3, called HLVM3, is to take the crew to about 400 km orbit.

q.s: Which one of the following statements about the PSLV is correct?
o: It cannot place satellites in sun-synchronous orbit
It uses a cryogenic upper stage
Its XL variant uses four strap-on motors
Its four stages are solid, liquid, solid and liquid
q.x: The PSLV has alternate solid and liquid stages and no cryogenic stage; PSLV-XL uses six extended strap-ons and can put about 1,750 kg in SSO.

q.s: The search-and-rescue transponders on INSAT satellites work under which international programme?
q.x: INSAT carries SAR payloads under COSPAS-SARSAT; Disaster Warning System uplinks are in C-band and downlinks in S-band.

q.s: EDUSAT, India's first satellite dedicated to education, was launched in 2004 by:
q.x: EDUSAT (GSAT-3) went up on GSLV-F01 on 20 September 2004 and provides two-way classroom links.

q.s: India's anti-satellite (ASAT) missile test 'Mission Shakti', which destroyed a satellite in low Earth orbit, was conducted in:
q.x: Mission Shakti (March 2019) hit a satellite at about 283 km so that the debris would decay quickly.

q.s: The formal threshold range above which a ballistic missile is classed as an Inter-Continental Ballistic Missile (ICBM) is:
q.x: The ICBM threshold is 5,500 km, so Agni-V (about 5,000 km) lies on the IRBM/ICBM border.

q.s: India joined the Missile Technology Control Regime (MTCR) in June 2016 as its:
q.x: India became the 35th member; the MTCR mainly covers missiles able to carry 500 kg over 300 km.

q.s: Which one of the following statements about the Missile Technology Control Regime is correct?
o: It mainly controls missiles able to carry 500 kg over 300 km
It is a treaty under the United Nations
In 1992 the USA sanctioned DRDO under it
q.x: The MTCR is an informal regime; India joined in 2016; the 1992 US sanctions were on ISRO and Glavkosmos.

q.s: 'e-Pathshala', the platform for digital textbooks, is run by:
q.x: e-Pathshala is NCERT's platform; Shiksha Vani is CBSE's podcast app.

q.s: 'Jeevan Pramaan' is an Aadhaar-based digital service that provides:
q.x: Jeevan Pramaan (2014) gives pensioners a Digital Life Certificate; Meri Pehchaan is the National Single Sign-On.

q.s: The UMANG app, launched in 2017, is meant to provide:
o: One app for central, state and local government services
Online payment of income tax only
q.x: UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) offers thousands of services in one app; DigiLocker stores documents.

q.s: Which of the following payment systems is operated by the Reserve Bank of India and NOT by the NPCI?
q.x: NEFT and RTGS are run by the RBI; IMPS, UPI, NACH, AePS and RuPay are NPCI systems.

q.s: 'EternalBlue', the Windows exploit used by the WannaCry ransomware of 2017, was originally developed by the:
q.x: EternalBlue was an NSA exploit leaked by the Shadow Brokers; WannaCry itself is attributed to North Korea's Lazarus group.

q.s: 'Pegasus' is an example of which type of malware?
q.x: Pegasus is spyware; Mirai is a botnet, Zeus a Trojan and Fireball adware.

q.s: Which of the following malware type–example pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: WannaCry was ransomware; Pegasus is the well-known spyware.

q.s: The Cyber Crisis Management Plan (CCMP) for countering cyber attacks and cyber terrorism has been framed by the:
q.x: The CCMP is a MeitY (CERT-In) framework followed by all governments; Cyber Jagrookta Diwas is run by MHA's I4C.

q.s: The atomic bomb 'Little Boy', dropped on Hiroshima, used which fissile material?
q.x: Little Boy used U-235 and Fat Man (Nagasaki) used Pu-239.

q.s: Who is known as the 'father of the hydrogen bomb'?
q.x: Edward Teller; Otto Hahn discovered nuclear fission (1938–39).

q.s: Apsara, which became critical in 1956, has the distinction of being:
o: India's and Asia's first research reactor
q.x: Apsara was the first research reactor in Asia; Dhruva (100 MW) is the largest and KAMINI runs on U-233.

q.s: Which of the following research reactors is NOT located at Trombay (BARC)?
q.x: KAMINI is at Kalpakkam, Tamil Nadu, and is the world's only U-233-fuelled reactor.

q.s: The Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG), originally called the 'London Club', was formed in 1975 in response to:
q.x: India's 1974 test prompted the NSG; India's membership bid since 2016 has been blocked mainly by China.

q.s: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the Nuclear Suppliers Group?
q.x: Iran is not among the NSG's 48 members; NSG membership is separate from the NPT.

q.s: Which of the following export-control regimes is India NOT yet a member of?
q.x: India joined the MTCR (2016), Wassenaar (2017) and Australia Group (2018), but not the NSG.

q.s: Under its updated NDC of August 2022, India committed to reduce the emission intensity of its GDP by 2030, from 2005 levels, by:
